text: 2 The attack on the king that has lost the right to castle
zh: 第二章　攻击失去易位权利的王

text: This situation arises when the king is either no longer able to castle or has been driven by the opponent away from the castling area. In spite of these possible differences of origin, the general picture and the problem involved are identical and ought to be dealt with in one and the same chapter.
zh: 这里所讨论的局面，既可能是王已经无法易位，也可能是王被对手赶离了易位后的藏身之处。虽然成因不同，但局面的基本特征和需要解决的问题是相同的，因此应当放在同一章中讨论。

text: First of all, it must be emphasized that the actual fact that a king has lost the right to castle does not necessarily always justify undertaking an attack aimed at mate (as will be shown by the examples of the voluntary loss of castling rights in chapter three). For an attack of this kind to be feasible, the loss of castling rights must at the same time involve the exposure of the king and an increased vulnerability to attack. In the majority of cases the attack is in fact in order, and we shall only consider such positive cases and not the rest. It only remains to be added that the loss of the right to castle can also entail a further weakness besides the danger which faces the king; that is, communication between the rooks is made more difficult. In fact, an attack may logically direct itself against this lack of co-operation between the rooks, e.g. in a struggle for control of an open file.
zh: 首先必须强调：王失去易位权利这一事实，本身并不总能成为发动将杀进攻的充分理由。第三章中主动放弃易位权利的例子会说明这一点。要使这种进攻成立，失去易位权利还必须伴随着王的暴露，以及王更容易受到攻击。在大多数情况下，发动进攻确实是合理的；本章只讨论这些可以进攻的局面，不讨论其余情况。另外，失去易位权利除了危及王的安全，还可能带来另一个弱点：两车之间更难取得联系。因此，把进攻的矛头指向两车配合不畅之处，也是顺理成章的，例如通过争夺开放线来利用这一弱点。

text:
We shall first examine a few typical examples portraying the drama of the king which has lost the right to castle. Such a drama can be divided up into the following episodes:
1) spoiling the king's castling chances, or drawing it away from the castling position;
2) the pursuit of the king across the board by checking; and
3) the final mating attack in the middle of the board or on the edge.
zh:
我们先看几个典型例子，看看失去易位权利的王会经历怎样一场戏剧。这场戏可以分为三幕：
1）破坏王的易位机会，或把王从易位后的藏身之处引出来；
2）连续将军，在棋盘上追赶王；
3）在棋盘中央或边缘完成最后的将杀进攻。

text: The following game is an illustration of just such a drama in three acts:
zh: 下面这盘棋正好展示了这样一场三幕剧：

text:
Potemkin – Alekhine
St Petersburg, 1912
Closed Sicilian
zh:
波将金—阿廖欣
1912年，圣彼得堡
西西里防御封闭变例

text: 1. e4 c5 2. g3 g6 3. Bg2 Bg7 4. Ne2 Nc6 5. c3 Nf6 6. Na3? d5 7. exd5 Nxd5 8. Nc2 O-O 9. d4 cxd4 10. cxd4 Bg4 11. f3 Bf5 12. Ne3 Qa5+
zh: 1. e4 c5 2. g3 g6 3. Bg2 Bg7 4. Ne2 Nc6 5. c3 Nf6 6. Na3? d5 7. exd5 Nxd5 8. Nc2 O-O 9. d4 cxd4 10. cxd4 Bg4 11. f3 Bf5 12. Ne3 Qa5+

text: The king is forced to move out of position (1st act).
zh: 王被迫离开原来的位置，第一幕就此上演。

text: Unavoidable, since if 13. Bd2, then 13... Nxe3 14. Bxa5 Nxd1, and Black wins a piece; this also happens after 13. Qd2 Nxe3 14. Qxa5 Nxg2+, etc.
zh: 别无选择，因为13. Bd2会遭到13... Nxe3 14. Bxa5 Nxd1，黑方得子；13. Qd2 Nxe3 14. Qxa5 Nxg2+等后续手段也有同样的结果。

text: 13... Ndb4 14. Nxf5 Qxf5 15. g4 Nd3+
zh: 13... Ndb4 14. Nxf5 Qxf5 15. g4 Nd3+

text: The second act (a short one) starts: the king has to move again. White decides on 16. Kg3?, a weak move, but even after the stronger 16. Kf1, Black retains the advantage with 16... Qb5.
zh: 短暂的第二幕开始了：王又必须移动。白方选择16. Kg3?，这是一步软着；但即使走较强的16. Kf1，黑方仍可用16... Qb5保持优势。

caption_zh: 白方走完16. Kg3后的局面

text: **16... Nxd4! 17. gxf5 Nxf5+ 0-1**, as Black mates in 2 moves: 18. Kg4 h5+ 19. Kh3 (or 19. Kg5 Bh6#) 19... Nf2#. (As an old chess player said on a similar occasion, “He's lucky to be mated, otherwise he would lose his queen...”).
zh: **16... Nxd4! 17. gxf5 Nxf5+ 0-1**，因为黑方有两步杀：18. Kg4 h5+ 19. Kh3（或19. Kg5 Bh6#）19... Nf2#。正如一位老棋手在类似场合开玩笑所说：“幸亏他被将杀了，否则就要失后了……”

text: We called hunting the king about the board “the second act of the drama”. However, it must be stressed that it is not the actual fact that the king has to move about that is of prime importance, but the extent to which its position is weakened. Instead of travelling all over the board it may happen that the king merely roams a little and gets itself tied up in a small space of two or three squares, while the opponent harries it with checks and thus manages to bring up his pieces with gain of time. A typical case where checks help to “nourish the development of the attack” arises in the following short game:
zh: 我们把在棋盘上追赶王称为“这场戏剧的第二幕”。不过，必须强调：最重要的不是王是否被迫四处移动，而是王的位置究竟被削弱了多少。王未必会走遍棋盘，也可能只在附近徘徊，最后被困在两三个格的小范围里；与此同时，对手不断将军，借此带着先手调集子力。下面这盘短局便是典型例子：连续将军为进攻的展开提供了养分。

text:
Clemens – Eisenschmidt
St Petersburg, 1890
Evans Gambit
zh:
克莱门斯—艾森施密特
1890年，圣彼得堡
埃文斯弃兵

text: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bxb4 5. c3 Bc5 6. d4 exd4 7. cxd4 Bb6 8. O-O d6 9. Nc3 Bd7? 10. e5 dxe5 11. Re1 Nge7 12. Ng5 (D)
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bxb4 5. c3 Bc5 6. d4 exd4 7. cxd4 Bb6 8. O-O d6 9. Nc3 Bd7? 10. e5 dxe5 11. Re1 Nge7 12. Ng5（见图）
caption_zh: 白方走完12. Ng5后的局面

text: Black gives up a pawn to get rid of the pressure on f7. Had he castled, then White would have won the exchange and a pawn by 13. Qh5.¹
zh: 黑方弃一兵，以解除f7承受的压力。如果此时易位，白方就能用13. Qh5得到半子和一兵。¹

text: ¹ Not so. After 13. Qh5 Bf5 White may have no advantage. 14. Nxf7 surprisingly fails to 14... Qxd4!, attacking both c4 and f2, when the discovered checks do not help White. Therefore White should try 14. Bxf7+ Kh8 15. dxe5, but even here 15... Qd4 16. Re3 Qg4 is unclear.
zh: ¹ 并非如此。13. Qh5 Bf5之后，白方未必有优势。令人意外的是，14. Nxf7会遭到14... Qxd4!，黑后同时攻击c4和f2，此时白方的闪将也无济于事。因此，白方应尝试14. Bxf7+ Kh8 15. dxe5，但即使如此，15... Qd4 16. Re3 Qg4后的局面仍不明朗。

text: 13. Bxe6 fxe6 14. Nxe6 Qd6 15. Nxg7+
zh: 13. Bxe6 fxe6 14. Nxe6 Qd6 15. Nxg7+

text: Black's king is prevented from castling.
zh: 黑王无法易位了。

caption_zh: 白方走完18. Ne6+后的局面

text: This check is followed by two more, as a result of which White's knights assume increasingly dangerous positions.
zh: 这次将军之后还有两次将军，白方的两匹马因此占据越来越危险的位置。

text: If 20... Kxf6, then 21. Qe6+, followed by mate in a few moves.
zh: 如果20... Kxf6，则21. Qe6+，再过几步就会将杀。

text: Excellent! White has a mating attack ready and needs only to get rid of Black's threat of ...Qxe1#.
zh: 好棋！白方的将杀进攻已经准备就绪，只需先解除黑方...Qxe1#的威胁。

text: This position is from the game Kotov–Bondarevsky, Leningrad 1936, when these future grandmasters were playing in a first-category tournament. Black, to move, directed the second and third acts of the drama as follows:
zh: 这是1936年在列宁格勒的科托夫对邦达列夫斯基一局。当时，这两位未来的特级大师正在参加一级棋手比赛。轮到黑方行棋，他以下列方式演绎了第二幕和第三幕：
caption_zh: 科托夫（白）对邦达列夫斯基（黑），黑方行棋

text: 1... f4+ 2. Nxf4 Qf2+ 3. Kd3 Qxd4+ 4. Kxd4 Bc5+ 5. Kd3 Nxe5#
zh: 1... f4+ 2. Nxf4 Qf2+ 3. Kd3 Qxd4+ 4. Kxd4 Bc5+ 5. Kd3 Nxe5#

text: This position is from the game Alekhine–Feldt, blindfold simultaneous display, Tarnopol 1916. White continued:
zh: 这是阿廖欣1916年在塔尔诺波尔举行蒙目车轮战时，对费尔特一局中的局面。白方接着走：
caption_zh: 阿廖欣（白）对费尔特（黑），白方行棋

text: **1. Nf7! Kxf7** (otherwise 2. Qxe6, etc.) **2. Qxe6+!** (drawing the king out still further; if 2... Kxe6, then 3. Ng5#) **2... Kg6 3. g4**, with mate next move by 4. Bxf5# or 4. Nh4#.
zh: **1. Nf7! Kxf7**（否则2. Qxe6等）**2. Qxe6+!**（进一步把王引出来；如果2... Kxe6，则3. Ng5#）**2... Kg6 3. g4**，下一步便有4. Bxf5#或4. Nh4#将杀。

text: Averbakh–Kotov, Zurich Ct 1953. In order to draw White's king out from the protection of its castled position, Black is prepared to give up his queen:
zh: 这是1953年苏黎世候选人赛中的阿韦尔巴赫对科托夫一局。为了把白王从易位后的庇护处引出来，黑方准备弃后：
caption_zh: 阿韦尔巴赫（白）对科托夫（黑），黑方行棋

text: **1... Qxh3+! 2. Kxh3 Rh6+ 3. Kg4 Nf6+ 4. Kf5 Nd7! 5. Rg5** (the only reply) **5... Rf8+ 6. Kg4 Nf6+ 7. Kf5 Ng8+ 8. Kg4 Nf6+ 9. Kf5 Nxd5+ 10. Kg4 Nf6+ 11. Kf5 Ng8+ 12. Kg4 Nf6+ 13. Kf5 Ng8+ 14. Kg4 Bxg5** (Black repeated moves because he was short of time, but now he proceeds to clear up the position) **15. Kxg5 Rf7! 16. Bh4 Rg6+ 17. Kh5 Rfg7 18. Bg5 Rxg5+ 19. Kh4 Nf6 20. Ng3 Rxg3 21. Qxd6 R3g6 22. Qb8+ Rg8 0-1**.
zh: **1... Qxh3+! 2. Kxh3 Rh6+ 3. Kg4 Nf6+ 4. Kf5 Nd7! 5. Rg5**（唯一的应对）**5... Rf8+ 6. Kg4 Nf6+ 7. Kf5 Ng8+ 8. Kg4 Nf6+ 9. Kf5 Nxd5+ 10. Kg4 Nf6+ 11. Kf5 Ng8+ 12. Kg4 Nf6+ 13. Kf5 Ng8+ 14. Kg4 Bxg5**（黑方由于时间紧张而重复走法，现在开始把局面处理清楚）**15. Kxg5 Rf7! 16. Bh4 Rg6+ 17. Kh5 Rfg7 18. Bg5 Rxg5+ 19. Kh4 Nf6 20. Ng3 Rxg3 21. Qxd6 R3g6 22. Qb8+ Rg8 0-1**。

text: From the game Gligorić–Petrosian, Belgrade 1954. White won as follows:
zh: 这是1954年在贝尔格莱德的格利戈里奇对彼得罗相一局。白方以下列方式获胜：
caption_zh: 格利戈里奇（白）对彼得罗相（黑），白方行棋

text: **1. Rxg5+ Kf7 2. Rxf6+ Kxf6 3. Qxf8+ Kxg5 4. h4+ 1-0**, since Black is faced with mate.
zh: **1. Rxg5+ Kf7 2. Rxf6+ Kxf6 3. Qxf8+ Kxg5 4. h4+ 1-0**，因为黑方面临将杀。

text: From the game D. Byrne–Fischer, New York Rosenwald 1957. Bobby Fischer, at the time a boy of thirteen, carried out an attack on the white king (which is no longer able to castle) by means of a brilliant queen sacrifice:
zh: 这是1957年纽约罗森瓦尔德赛中的D.伯恩对菲舍尔一局。当时年仅十三岁的鲍比·菲舍尔，以漂亮的弃后，向已经无法易位的白王发动进攻：
caption_zh: D.伯恩（白）对菲舍尔（黑），黑方行棋

text: **1... Be6! 2. Bxb6** (if 2. Qxc3, then 2... Qxc5, while if 2. Bxe6, then 2... Qb5+) **2... Bxc4+ 3. Kg1 Ne2+ 4. Kf1 Nxd4+ 5. Kg1 Ne2+ 6. Kf1 Nc3+ 7. Kg1 axb6 8. Qb4 Ra4 9. Qxb6 Nxd1**, and Black won on the basis of his material superiority.
zh: **1... Be6! 2. Bxb6**（如果2. Qxc3，则2... Qxc5；如果2. Bxe6，则2... Qb5+）**2... Bxc4+ 3. Kg1 Ne2+ 4. Kf1 Nxd4+ 5. Kg1 Ne2+ 6. Kf1 Nc3+ 7. Kg1 axb6 8. Qb4 Ra4 9. Qxb6 Nxd1**，黑方凭借子力优势取得胜利。

text: The pursuit of a king that has lost the right to castle is not, however, always such a successful undertaking as in the examples quoted. There have in fact been many occasions when the hunted king has come out the winner by successfully escaping to safety, and when the whole of his flight turns out in the end to be artificial castling on a large scale!
zh: 不过，追赶失去易位权利的王，并不总能像上述例子那样成功。实际上，许多被追赶的王最终逃到了安全地带，其一方反而赢得了对局；回头看，王的整段逃亡不过是一次大规模的人工易位！

text: A player who is pursuing a king in such circumstances must therefore keep his eyes open to make sure that the prey does not elude him. Two factors are particularly important: the tempo of the attack and slowly but surely building up a mating net from which the king has no escape. As a matter of fact, this net is often of more importance than tempi, and quiet moves which “spin the threads” often point the correct way, whereas many juicy checks may prove to be mistakes. The position of the king that has lost the right to castle represents, as it were, the attacker's capital, which he has acquired at the price of sacrifices or positional disadvantages. The attacker should retain his hold on this capital without worrying too much about “short-term gains” in the form of tempting checks; the decisive point in the end is whether the king is going to fall or not.
zh: 因此，在这种情况下追赶王的一方必须保持警觉，防止猎物逃脱。有两个因素尤其重要：进攻中的先手，以及逐步织成一道让王无路可逃的杀网。事实上，杀网往往比先手更重要；那些悄悄“织网”的安静走法，常常才是正确的方向，而许多看似诱人的将军却可能是错误。失去易位权利的王所处的位置，好比进攻方的本钱，是他以弃子或位置上的不利为代价换来的。进攻方应当握住这份本钱，不必过于计较那些诱人的将军所带来的“眼前收益”；最终具有决定意义的，是能否把王将杀。

text: These remarks are intended to inspire the reader to be cautious in his pursuit of a king that has lost the right to castle. Two maxims here oppose each other: the first instructs one to keep up the tempo of the attack by means of checks in order to give the king no time to recover its breath; the second warns that it is important to finish off the pursuit by cornering the king and forcing it into a mating position. In practice players struggle to find a balance between these two maxims and on their correct choice success itself depends.
zh: 这些提醒，是希望读者在追赶失去易位权利的王时保持谨慎。这里有两条彼此牵制的准则：第一条要求用连续将军保持进攻的先手，不给王喘息的时间；第二条提醒我们，必须最终把王逼入绝境，迫使它落入将杀局面，才能结束追击。实战中，棋手需要在这两条准则之间找到平衡；能否作出正确选择，决定着进攻的成败。

text: Now that the problem is clear, it will be examined in a series of practical examples. Smyslov–Florian and Belavenets–Chistiakov are cases where the building of a mating net takes precedence over the pursuit of the king. In Tartakower–Euwe, however, we shall see the opposite, with Euwe hunting his opponent's king without giving it a moment's respite. In the game Chigorin–Caro we have an illustration of when a king's pursuit should be halted and its retreat cut off, or, conversely, what happens if an opportunity to “fix” the king is lost and it reaches a position of safety, as in fact occurred in this game.
zh: 问题已经明确，下面通过一系列实战例子来考察。斯梅斯洛夫对弗洛里安、别拉韦涅茨对奇斯佳科夫这两局，都表明织杀网比追赶王更重要。塔塔科维尔对尤伟一局则相反：尤伟追赶对手的王，丝毫不给它喘息的机会。齐果林对卡罗一局说明，应当在什么时候停止追赶、转而切断王的退路；反过来，如果错过了把王困住的机会，让它逃到了安全地带，又会怎样——这盘棋实际发生的正是后一种情况。

text:
Smyslov – Florian
Moscow–Budapest Match 1949
Grünfeld Defence
zh:
斯梅斯洛夫—弗洛里安
1949年，莫斯科—布达佩斯对抗赛
格林菲尔德防御

text: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Nf3 Bg7 5. Qb3 dxc4 6. Qxc4 O-O 7. e4 Na6 8. Be2 c5 9. d5 e6 10. O-O exd5 11. exd5 Qa5 12. a3 Bf5 13. Qh4 Rfe8 14. Bh6 Ne4 15. Bxg7 Kxg7 (D)
zh: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Nf3 Bg7 5. Qb3 dxc4 6. Qxc4 O-O 7. e4 Na6 8. Be2 c5 9. d5 e6 10. O-O exd5 11. exd5 Qa5 12. a3 Bf5 13. Qh4 Rfe8 14. Bh6 Ne4 15. Bxg7 Kxg7（见图）
caption_zh: 黑方走完15... Kxg7后的局面

text: White offers a piece in order to keep up the tempo of the attack. Black should now have played 16... Nxg5, for after 17. Qxg5 his position would only have been slightly inferior. Instead, he became greedy and replied:
zh: 白方提出弃子，以保持进攻中的先手。黑方此时应走16... Nxg5，因为17. Qxg5之后，黑方只是略处下风。但他贪心地走了：

text: White does not hurry with his action against the displaced king, but calmly takes the knight and waits for the mating network to develop of itself.
zh: 白方并不急着追击已经离开庇护处的王，而是从容吃掉马，等待杀网逐渐成形。

caption_zh: 黑方走完18... Kxg5后的局面

text: Black loses quickly. The most effective reply would have been 18... Rxe2 19. f4 Rf8!¹. Other variations, which all lead to the effective construction of a mating net, are:
zh: 黑方很快就输了。最有效的应对本是18... Rxe2 19. f4 Rf8!¹。其余变化都让白方能够有效地织成杀网：

text: 1) 18... Rxe2 19. f4 Qc7 20. d6 Qd7 21. Rae1 Bd3 (if 21... Rae8 then 22. Rxe2 Rxe2 23. Qh8#) 22. Rxe2 Bxe2 23. Re1 Bc4 (otherwise 24. Re7) 24. Ne4+, etc.
zh: 1）18... Rxe2 19. f4 Qc7 20. d6 Qd7 21. Rae1 Bd3（如果21... Rae8，则22. Rxe2 Rxe2 23. Qh8#）22. Rxe2 Bxe2 23. Re1 Bc4（否则24. Re7）24. Ne4+等。

text: 2) 18... Rh8 19. Qxf7+ Kxg5 20. Qg7! (depriving the king of the square h6; 20. f4+? Kh6 is wrong) 20... Kf4 21. Rae1². Here again White does not put Black in check but instead prevents the king from using the e-file; if 21... Ke4 White mates with 22. Bc4+ Kf4 23. g3+, etc.
zh: 2）18... Rh8 19. Qxf7+ Kxg5 20. Qg7!（不让王走到h6；20. f4+? Kh6反而不对）20... Kf4 21. Rae1²。白方这里同样没有将军，而是封住王通往e线的道路；如果21... Ke4，则白方用22. Bc4+ Kf4 23. g3+等手段将杀。

text: A quiet move, cutting off the king's retreat and preparing for mate with 20. f4+, etc.
zh: 安静的一步，切断王的退路，并准备以20. f4+等手段将杀。

text: 19... Re4 20. f4+ Rxf4 21. Rxf4 Kxf4 22. Rf1+ Ke3
zh: 19... Re4 20. f4+ Rxf4 21. Rxf4 Kxf4 22. Rf1+ Ke3

text: If 22... Kg5 then 23. h4+ leads to mate, or if 22... Ke4, a mating net is formed by 23. Bc4.
zh: 如果22... Kg5，则23. h4+后将杀；如果22... Ke4，白方以23. Bc4织成杀网。

text: 23. Qe5+ Kd2
zh: 23. Qe5+ Kd2

text: Well may he run – mate is not far off.
zh: 任它怎么逃，也离将杀不远了。

text: It is mate in two more moves.
zh: 再过两步就会将杀。

text: ¹ Although Smyslov then gives the continuation 20. Qh6 Rfe8 21. Rae1 Bd3 22. Qh4 Ke7 23. Ne4+ Kf8 24. d6 Kg7 25. f5, with a decisive attack for White.
zh: ¹ 不过，斯梅斯洛夫给出的后续手段是20. Qh6 Rfe8 21. Rae1 Bd3 22. Qh4 Ke7 23. Ne4+ Kf8 24. d6 Kg7 25. f5，白方获得决定性的进攻。

text: ² It is even simpler to mate with checks by 21. g3+ Ke4 22. Qe7+ Kxd5 23. Bc4+ Kc6 24. Bf3+, etc.
zh: ² 更简单的办法是连续将军：21. g3+ Ke4 22. Qe7+ Kxd5 23. Bc4+ Kc6 24. Bf3+等，最后将杀。

text:
Belavenets – Chistiakov
Semi-finals, USSR Ch 1938
French Defence, McCutcheon Variation
zh:
别拉韦涅茨—奇斯佳科夫
1938年，苏联锦标赛半决赛
法兰西防御，麦卡琴变例

text: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Bb4
zh: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Bb4

text: The so-called McCutcheon Variation, which is nowadays regarded as unfavourable for Black.
zh: 这就是所谓的麦卡琴变例，在作者写作时被认为对黑方不利。

text: 5. e5 h6 6. Bd2 Bxc3 7. bxc3 Ne4 8. Qg4 g6 9. Bd3
zh: 5. e5 h6 6. Bd2 Bxc3 7. bxc3 Ne4 8. Qg4 g6 9. Bd3

text: 9. Bc1 is also possible, to enable the bishop to exert pressure from a3. In this position it does not matter to White that he loses the right to castle, but he must play sharply and accurately, as otherwise Black's attack along the c-file may prevail.
zh: 也可以走9. Bc1，让象从a3施加压力。在这个局面中，失去易位权利对白方并不重要，但他必须走得积极而准确，否则黑方沿c线的进攻可能占上风。

text: Maroczy's move, 11. h4, is an alternative.
zh: 另一种选择是马洛契的走法11. h4。

text: A poor move. 12. Rab1 was preferable.¹
zh: 这步不好，12. Rab1更可取。¹

text: ¹ According to current theory both 12. Rab1 and 12. Qf4 give White a slight advantage.
zh: ¹ 按照编者写作时的理论，12. Rab1和12. Qf4都能使白方取得略微优势。

text: Note how Black plays from here up to his 15th move. He does not pursue the unfruitful plan of “looking for checks” with 12... cxd4? 13. cxd4 Qa5+, but quietly brings his rook on to the c-file; then, and only then, does he strike by means of ...cxd4.
zh: 请注意黑方从这里到第15回合的走法。他没有采用12... cxd4? 13. cxd4 Qa5+这种毫无成效的“寻找将军”的计划，而是先安静地把车调到c线上；等这一切准备妥当，才以...cxd4出击。

text: 13. Qh4 Bd7 14. Qf6 Rg8 15. h4 Rc8 16. h5 gxh5 17. Qxh6 cxd4 18. cxd4 (D)
zh: 13. Qh4 Bd7 14. Qf6 Rg8 15. h4 Rc8 16. h5 gxh5 17. Qxh6 cxd4 18. cxd4（见图）
caption_zh: 白方走完18. cxd4后的局面

text: Now begins a well-prepared attack on the king, which has already been drawn out of position.
zh: 现在，针对已经被引离原位的王，一场准备充分的进攻开始了。

text: 19. Nxd4 Qc3+ 20. Ke3 Rc4 21. Qf4 Rg4 22. Ne2 Re4+ 0-1
zh: 19. Nxd4 Qc3+ 20. Ke3 Rc4 21. Qf4 Rg4 22. Ne2 Re4+ 0-1

text: This position arose in the game Tartakower–Euwe, Venice 1948. It is Black's move; first of all, he draws the king out from his castled position by a sacrifice:
zh: 这是1948年在威尼斯的塔塔科维尔对尤伟一局中的局面。轮到黑方行棋；他先用弃子把王从易位后的庇护处引出来：
caption_zh: 塔塔科维尔（白）对尤伟（黑），黑方行棋

text: The king must come out, since 3. Kg1 would be answered by the still more unpleasant 3... gxf4 4. Bc5 Qg7 5. Kh1 Bf1+ 6. Nh2 Qh7.
zh: 王必须出来，因为3. Kg1会遭到更难受的3... gxf4 4. Bc5 Qg7 5. Kh1 Bf1+ 6. Nh2 Qh7。

text: 3... gxf4+ 4. Bxf4 Qd7
zh: 3... gxf4+ 4. Bxf4 Qd7

text: At first all is quiet, but then comes the storm.
zh: 起初一切平静，随后风暴袭来。

text: 5. Nh2 exf4+ 6. Kxf4 Rh4+ 7. Ke3
zh: 5. Nh2 exf4+ 6. Kxf4 Rh4+ 7. Ke3

text: If 7. Kf3, then 7... Bg2+!, or if 7. Kg3, then 7... Rg4+!.
White is not to be allowed a respite! 8... Rh3 9. Be2 Qg4 would have been unclear owing to 10. Rg1.
zh: 不能让白方喘息！8... Rh3 9. Be2 Qg4后，由于白方有10. Rg1，局面反而不明朗。

text: 9. Kxe4 Nd6+
zh: 9. Kxe4 Nd6+

text: Now Black captures two pieces en route by a series of checks.
zh: 现在黑方通过一连串将军，在追王的途中顺便吃掉两个子。

text: If 12. Kc5, then 12... Qxc4+ 13. Kxd6 Qd5+ 14. Ke7 Rg8 and mate.¹
zh: 如果12. Kc5，则12... Qxc4+ 13. Kxd6 Qd5+ 14. Ke7 Rg8，随后将杀。¹

text: ¹ Surprisingly, this line is not entirely clear after 15. Nh4+ Kh7 16. Nf5! Qxf5 17. Rad1. The simplest win after 12. Kc5 is 12... Nxc4 13. Qxb7 Qd6+ 14. Kxc4 Qd5+ 15. Kb4 c5+, winning the queen.
zh: ¹ 令人意外的是，15. Nh4+ Kh7 16. Nf5! Qxf5 17. Rad1之后，这个变化并不完全清楚。对12. Kc5，最简单的取胜办法是12... Nxc4 13. Qxb7 Qd6+ 14. Kxc4 Qd5+ 15. Kb4 c5+，黑方得后。

text: White, by allowing himself to be “bled”, has obtained a little breathing space, but not for long.
zh: 白方付出子力上的代价，换来了一点喘息的余地，但好景不长。

text: Black's king is in a safe enough position after 17. Qc7+ Ke6.
zh: 17. Qc7+ Ke6之后，黑王的位置足够安全。

caption_zh: 白方走完18. Ka3后的局面

text: The storm has regained its force once more; the end is not far off.
zh: 风暴再次猛烈起来，结局已经不远。

text: 19. bxc4 Rxa4+ 20. Kxa4 Qa2+ 21. Kb4 Qb2+ 0-1
zh: 19. bxc4 Rxa4+ 20. Kxa4 Qa2+ 21. Kb4 Qb2+ 0-1

text: For if 22. Kc5, then 22... Qxf2+, and White loses his queen; or if 22. Ka5, then 22... Qa3#. A fine example of a consistent pursuit of the king.
zh: 因为如果22. Kc5，则22... Qxf2+，白方失后；如果22. Ka5，则22... Qa3#。这是坚持追王的一个精彩例子。

text: The following unusual game, which dates from long ago, gave rise to amusement at the tournament itself and only superficial comments in the tournament book. Chess books concerned themselves with the game no further, and in doing so let slip some fine material with which to illustrate the theme of “the king's wanderings and flight”. Only with the commentary below, containing a discussion of the king's journey and an exposition of the technique of “net-building”, has this game been placed in correct perspective.
zh: 下面这盘久远而奇特的对局，当时在赛场上引来不少笑谈，赛会对局集也只给出了肤浅的评论。此后的棋书没有再深入研究它，因而错过了一份展示“王的游走与逃亡”的好材料。下面的评注讨论王的行程，并阐述“织网”的技巧，这才使我们能够恰当地理解这盘棋。

text:
Chigorin – Caro
Vienna, 1898
Vienna Game
zh:
齐果林—卡罗
1898年，维也纳
维也纳开局

text: Theory discarded this move long ago, since Black, by sacrificing his knight on e4, can obtain at least a draw. Correct is 4. fxe5.¹
zh: 理论早已否定了这步棋，因为黑方可以在e4弃马，至少取得和棋。正确的是4. fxe5。¹

text: ¹ 4. fxe5 usually transposes to the game continuation after 4... Nxe4 5. d3 Bb4. White has other possibilities at move 5, but none gives him any advantage.
zh: ¹ 4. fxe5 Nxe4 5. d3 Bb4通常转入实战的后续手段。白方在第5步还有其他选择，但都不能带来优势。

text: 4... Bb4 5. fxe5 Nxe4 6. dxe4 Qh4+ 7. Ke2
zh: 4... Bb4 5. fxe5 Nxe4 6. dxe4 Qh4+ 7. Ke2

text: The king, having lost the right to castle, takes the first step on its long journey, which is to end on the square a1!
zh: 王失去了易位权利，踏上漫长旅途的第一站；这趟旅程最终竟会在a1结束！

text: 7... Bxc3 8. bxc3 Bg4+ 9. Nf3 dxe4 10. Qd4 Bh5! 11. Ke3 Bxf3 12. Bb5+
zh: 7... Bxc3 8. bxc3 Bg4+ 9. Nf3 dxe4 10. Qd4 Bh5! 11. Ke3 Bxf3 12. Bb5+

text: A risky move, first played by Steinitz against Blackburne in 1876. Correct here is 12. gxf3 on which Black can get a draw with 12... Qe1+ 13. Kf4 Qh4+, etc. Chigorin, in playing 12. Bb5+, avoids this possibility, for a draw was naturally not to his liking.
zh: 这是冒险的一步，斯坦尼茨1876年对布莱克本时首先采用了它。这里正确的是12. gxf3，黑方可用12... Qe1+ 13. Kf4 Qh4+等手段取得和棋。齐果林走12. Bb5+，正是为了避开这种可能性，因为他当然不甘心和棋。

caption_zh: 白方走完13. gxf3后的局面

text: The co-creator of the Caro-Kann Defence departs from the theory of his time and hits on the very best move. The theoreticians of the day rejected it, probably because Caro lost the game, and noted in their books that Black obtains the advantage by continuing 13... cxb5 14. Qxe4 Qxe4+ 15. Kxe4 O-O 16. Be3 Nd7. However, it seems that these old masters either examined this position by feeble gas-light or else they supposed that White would now have to succumb by playing 17. Rad1? Nxe5 18. Kxe5 Rfe8+ 19. Kf4 g5+. However, by modern reckoning White would have the better game, if he were to play consistently for a central position with 17. Bd4. In view of the threat of 18. Rab1 a6 19. a4, Black's best reply is 17... a6; then there follows 18. Rhg1 with the intention of weakening Black's position on the long dark diagonal.
zh: 卡罗—卡恩防御的这位共同创立者，偏离了当时的理论，却找到了最佳的一步。当时的理论家否定了这步棋，或许只是因为卡罗输掉了对局；他们在书中写道，13... cxb5 14. Qxe4 Qxe4+ 15. Kxe4 O-O 16. Be3 Nd7可以使黑方取得优势。然而，这些老大师似乎不是在昏暗的煤气灯下看错了局面，就是以为白方只能走17. Rad1? Nxe5 18. Kxe5 Rfe8+ 19. Kf4 g5+，然后败下阵来。按照作者所处时代的认识，如果白方坚持把子力放在中心，走17. Bd4，局面反而更好。面对18. Rab1 a6 19. a4的威胁，黑方最好走17... a6；随后18. Rhg1，白方打算削弱黑方在黑格长斜线上的防守。

text: 14. Kxe4
zh: 14. Kxe4

text: Chigorin takes a further risk; 14. Ke2 would have been good enough for a draw after 14... Qh3 (not 14... exf3+ on account of 15. Kf2 Qh3 16. Bf1!) 15. Rd1 exf3+ (15... Qxf3+ is weak, because of 16. Ke1! and White saves his bishop) 16. Kf2 Qxh2+ 17. Ke3 Qh6+ with perpetual check (for if 18. Ke4 Qh4+ 19. Bf4, Black can play 19... cxb5).
zh: 齐果林进一步冒险。14. Ke2本来足以取得和棋：14... Qh3（不能14... exf3+，因为15. Kf2 Qh3 16. Bf1!）15. Rd1 exf3+（15... Qxf3+较弱，因为16. Ke1!后白方可以保住象）16. Kf2 Qxh2+ 17. Ke3 Qh6+，形成长将。如果18. Ke4 Qh4+ 19. Bf4，黑方则可以19... cxb5。

text: 14... Qg6+ 15. Ke3 cxb5 16. Ba3 Nc6 17. Qd5 Qxc2 18. Rac1 Qf5 19. Rhe1 Rd8?! (D)
zh: 14... Qg6+ 15. Ke3 cxb5 16. Ba3 Nc6 17. Qd5 Qxc2 18. Rac1 Qf5 19. Rhe1 Rd8?!（见图）
caption_zh: 黑方走完19... Rd8后的局面

text: Black clearly cannot take the e-pawn because of 20. Kf2, but 19... b4 would have been better and safer than the move played. After 20. Bxb4 (20. cxb4 O-O 21. b5 Rfe8 is in Black's favour) 20... Nxb4 21. cxb4 O-O the exposed position of White's king together with his scattered pawns gives Black a considerable advantage. Thus in the event of 22. Red1 (22. Rc7 is weaker because of 22... Rae8 23. f4 Rd8 24. Qe4 Qh3+) 22... Rae8 23. f4 Qh3+ 24. Qf3 Qxh2 25. Rd2 Qh6 Black threatens both 26... Rxe5+ and 26... f6. The queen's great manoeuvrability comes into its own in situations like this.
zh: 由于20. Kf2，黑方显然不能吃e兵；但19... b4比实战走法更好，也更稳妥。20. Bxb4（20. cxb4 O-O 21. b5 Rfe8对白方不利）20... Nxb4 21. cxb4 O-O之后，白王暴露，白兵分散，黑方获得相当大的优势。例如22. Red1（22. Rc7较弱，因为22... Rae8 23. f4 Rd8 24. Qe4 Qh3+）22... Rae8 23. f4 Qh3+ 24. Qf3 Qxh2 25. Rd2 Qh6，黑方同时威胁26... Rxe5+和26... f6。在这样的局面中，后灵活转移的能力可以充分发挥。

text: 20. Qxb5
zh: 20. Qxb5

text: 20. Bd6 also came into consideration, though 20... f6 would then have led to a difficult and unclear position.
zh: 20. Bd6也值得考虑，不过20... f6之后，局面会复杂而不明朗。

text: 20... g5 could have been parried by 21. Rcd1.
zh: 20... g5可以用21. Rcd1应付。

text: The queen must cover the d3-square and if 21. Qf1, then Black could have carried out an artificial castling by means of ...Kd7-c8 and so made his advantage clear.¹
zh: 后必须照应d3格。如果21. Qf1，黑方就可以通过...Kd7-c8完成人工易位，使优势变得明确。¹

text: ¹ In fact 21. Qf1 Kd7 can be met by 22. Qd3+ and White escapes into a playable ending. 21. Qf1 is best answered by 21... Nxe5 and White cannot exploit the line-up on the e-file because his own king is so exposed.
zh: ¹ 实际上，21. Qf1 Kd7可以用22. Qd3+应对，白方得以转入尚可一战的残局。对21. Qf1，最好走21... Nxe5；白王自身太暴露，无法利用e线上黑方子力排成一线的机会。

text: White has to consent to this move, which exposes his king still further; 22. Kf2? is not good on account of 22... Qh4+ 23. Kf1 (neither 23. Ke3 Qh6+ nor 23. Kg1 Rd2 is any better) 23... Qh3+ 24. Kf2 Qxh2+ 25. Ke3 Qd2+ 26. Ke4 g5 and Black wins.
zh: 白方不得不走这一步，让王进一步暴露。22. Kf2?不好，因为22... Qh4+ 23. Kf1（23. Ke3 Qh6+和23. Kg1 Rd2都无济于事）23... Qh3+ 24. Kf2 Qxh2+ 25. Ke3 Qd2+ 26. Ke4 g5，黑方获胜。

text: If 23. Qe4 then 23... Qxa2! 24. Bd6 Kd7 and Black succeeds in consolidating the position of his king while remaining a pawn ahead. Also interesting is 23. Qc2 Qh3+ 24. Ke4 f5+ 25. exf6 gxf6. The opening up of the e-file is of no help to White, since his king has nowhere to go; in view of the threat of mate he is forced to play 26. f5, on which 26... Ne5 wins.
zh: 如果23. Qe4，则23... Qxa2! 24. Bd6 Kd7，黑方在保持多一兵的同时，也使王的位置稳固下来。23. Qc2 Qh3+ 24. Ke4 f5+ 25. exf6 gxf6也很有意思。打开e线对白方没有帮助，因为白王无处可去；面对将杀威胁，他被迫走26. f5，而26... Ne5后黑方获胜。

text: To engineer a possible escape for the king via d2 White would have to give up his h-pawn; moreover, there would also be a permanent danger of the exchange of queens. For this reason he prefers to embark on new adventures.
zh: 白方若想安排王经d2逃走，就必须放弃h兵；此外，还会始终面临兑后的危险。因此，他宁可开始新的冒险。

caption_zh: 白方走完25. Kd5后的局面

text: This position caused amazement among some of the spectators, who attempted to get the manager of the tournament to intervene, since it was clear that White's piece on d5 was his queen and that on b1 his king! The position is, of course, a strange one; what is also unusual is that within seven moves the white king has reached a1. Clearly, it is helped in this by Black, who checks unnecessarily instead of building up a mating net. Black played 25... Qg2+?, when the correct move was 25... Rc8!. In that case White's king would get into trouble on the c-file, which it would have to cross to extract itself from the scrape it has got into. The following variations illustrate the strength of the rook move and are at the same time instructive as regards play against an exposed king: 25... Rc8! and now:
zh: 一些观众看到这个局面十分惊讶，甚至想请赛事负责人出面干预，因为在他们看来，白方d5上的显然应该是后，b1上的才应该是王！这个局面当然很奇特；更奇特的是，仅仅七步之后，白王便到了a1。黑方显然帮了它的忙：他没有织杀网，却不断作出不必要的将军。黑方走了25... Qg2+?，正确的却是25... Rc8!。这样一来，白王想脱身就必须穿过c线，并会在那里遇到麻烦。下面这些变化既说明了这步动车的力量，也展示了怎样对付暴露的王。25... Rc8!之后：

text: 1) White carries out a counterattack with his queen: 26. Qxb7 Qg2+ 27. Kc5 Ne7+ 28. Kb6 Rc6+ 29. Ka7 Qf2+ 30. Ka8 O-O+ 31. Bb8 Rb6 and Black wins.
zh: 1）白方用后反击：26. Qxb7 Qg2+ 27. Kc5 Ne7+ 28. Kb6 Rc6+ 29. Ka7 Qf2+ 30. Ka8 O-O+ 31. Bb8 Rb6，黑方获胜。

text: 2) The white king tries to force its way through to the a1-corner; this gives rise to the most interesting point in the analysis. After 26. Kc4 Black does not try any checking moves, but instead first consolidates his own position by 26... g6!!, having observed that White has no good move to make. If 27. Rc2 or 27. Qc2, then 27... b5+ 28. Kb3 Nd4+, while if 27. Rcd1, then 27... Nd4+; if 27. Red1 or 27. Rf1, the ring is tightened by 27... Qe3, and if 27. Qb6, then 27... Na5+ 28. Kd5 (or 28. Kb4 Qxh2!) 28... Qg2+ 29. Ke6 Qxa2+ 30. Kf6 (or 30. c4 Nxc4, etc.) 30... Rc6 31. Qa7 Rf8+ 32. Kg7 Rc7+! 33. Bxc7 Rg8+ 34. Kf6 Qf7+ 35. Kg5 Qe7+ and mates.¹
zh: 2）白王试图闯到a1角落，这带出了分析中最有趣的一点。26. Kc4之后，黑方不急于将军，而是先用26... g6!!巩固自身局面，因为他已经看出白方没有好棋可走。如果27. Rc2或27. Qc2，则27... b5+ 28. Kb3 Nd4+；如果27. Rcd1，则27... Nd4+；如果27. Red1或27. Rf1，则用27... Qe3进一步收紧包围圈；如果27. Qb6，则27... Na5+ 28. Kd5（或28. Kb4 Qxh2!）28... Qg2+ 29. Ke6 Qxa2+ 30. Kf6（或30. c4 Nxc4等）30... Rc6 31. Qa7 Rf8+ 32. Kg7 Rc7+! 33. Bxc7 Rg8+ 34. Kf6 Qf7+ 35. Kg5 Qe7+，随后将杀。¹

text: The possibility of 27. Kb3 still remains. There is admittedly no mating net then, but with 27... Qxh2 Black obtains a material advantage and goes on to threaten both 28... Qxf4 and 28... Na5+ followed by ...Nc4.
zh: 白方还可以27. Kb3。诚然，这样没有现成的杀网，但黑方用27... Qxh2获得子力优势，随后同时威胁28... Qxf4，以及28... Na5+后接...Nc4。

text: 3) The white king tries to defy the danger of mate by advancing to b6. Black then has a number of continuations, the simplest of which seems to be 26. Kc5 Qxh2 27. Kb6 Qxf4 28. Kxb7 (if 28. Qb3, then 28... Qf2+ 29. Bc5 Qxc5+ 30. Kxc5 Na5+ with a won ending) 28... Qc4 29. Kxc8 Nb4+ 30. Kb7 Qb5+ 31. Ka7 Nc6+ followed by 32... Kd7+ and mates.
zh: 3）白王试图走到b6，迎着将杀的危险继续前进。黑方有多种后续手段，最简单的似乎是26. Kc5 Qxh2 27. Kb6 Qxf4 28. Kxb7（如果28. Qb3，则28... Qf2+ 29. Bc5 Qxc5+ 30. Kxc5 Na5+，进入胜势残局）28... Qc4 29. Kxc8 Nb4+ 30. Kb7 Qb5+ 31. Ka7 Nc6+，随后32... Kd7+并将杀。

text: ¹ In this line Vuković fails to take his own advice and gives too many checks, which actually allow White to escape by 34. Kh6! Qxh2+ 35. Kg5 Qg3+ 36. Kf6, etc. The correct continuation is 32... Qe6! and there is no way to meet the threat of 33... Rg8+ 34. Kh6 g5+.
zh: ¹ 在这个变化中，武科维奇没有遵循自己的建议，给出了太多将军，实际上让白方可以通过34. Kh6! Qxh2+ 35. Kg5 Qg3+ 36. Kf6等手段逃脱。正确的后续手段是32... Qe6!，白方无法应付33... Rg8+ 34. Kh6 g5+的威胁。

text: The actual game took the following course:
zh: 实战则这样进行：

caption_zh: 黑方走完29... Rc8后的局面

text: White obviously cannot play 30. Qxf5 since then 30... Na5+ leads to mate; instead, he gives up his f-pawn and then by retreating his king quickly to a1 safeguards his position.
zh: 白方显然不能30. Qxf5，因为30... Na5+后会被将杀。他放弃f兵，再迅速把王退到a1，保障自身局面的安全。

text: A further mistake; he could still have fought for a draw by 32... Qf3!. The square c4 is naturally more suitable for the knight.
zh: 又一次失误；32... Qf3!本来仍可争取和棋。c4格自然更适合马来占据。

text: After 33... Rc6 34. Qd1 Nb7 35. Be5 Black cannot play 35... Rxe6 because of 36. Bxg7 Rg8 37. Rxe6+ and White wins.
zh: 33... Rc6 34. Qd1 Nb7 35. Be5之后，黑方不能35... Rxe6，因为36. Bxg7 Rg8 37. Rxe6+，白方获胜。

text: A terrible move; he should have played 34... Rd8.
zh: 糟糕的一步；应当走34... Rd8。

text: Since if 36... Rxg7, then 37. Qxh5+ followed by 38. Qh8+ and White forces mate.
zh: 因为如果36... Rxg7，则37. Qxh5+后接38. Qh8+，白方强制将杀。

text: In addition to this strange game, I shall extract from the treasury of chess curiosities three more encounters which have particular relevance to the theme of a king's successful wandering. The series opens with a game between Hamppe and Meitner, in which the pursued king seeks asylum among the enemy pawns and is successful to the extent that the opponent cannot obtain anything beyond perpetual check.
zh: 除了这盘奇特的对局，我还要从国际象棋的奇闻宝库中选出三局，它们尤其切合王游走后成功脱险的主题。首先是汉佩对迈特纳一局：被追赶的王跑到敌方兵群中寻求庇护，成功到让对手除了长将之外，再也无计可施。

text:
Hamppe – Meitner
Vienna, 1872
Vienna Game
zh:
汉佩—迈特纳
1872年，维也纳
维也纳开局

text: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Bc5 3. Na4
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Bc5 3. Na4

text: 3. Nf3, which was often played by Anderssen, is the soundest answer to 2... Bc5. Hamppe's move is of doubtful value because of the bishop sacrifice on f2.
zh: 安德森经常采用的3. Nf3，是对2... Bc5最稳健的应对。由于黑方可以在f2弃象，汉佩这步棋的价值值得怀疑。

text: In return for the bishop, Black obtains a promising attack on the king, which is deprived of the right to castle.
zh: 黑方以一象为代价，使白王失去易位权利，并获得有希望的进攻。

text: 4. Kxf2 Qh4+ 5. Ke3
zh: 4. Kxf2 Qh4+ 5. Ke3

text: If 5. g3 then 5... Qxe4 6. Qe2 Qxa4 (not 6... Qxh1 because of 7. Nf3 and 8. Bg2) 7. Qxe5+ Ne7 8. Qxg7 Rg8 9. Qxh7 d6 and Black has the better position.
zh: 如果5. g3，则5... Qxe4 6. Qe2 Qxa4（不能6... Qxh1，因为7. Nf3后接8. Bg2）7. Qxe5+ Ne7 8. Qxg7 Rg8 9. Qxh7 d6，黑方局面较好。

caption_zh: 黑方走完6... d5后的局面

text: 7. Kc3
zh: 7. Kc3

text: White plans b3 and Kb2. If 7. Nc3, then 7... Nf6! 8. Qe1 (or 8. Qf3 dxe4+ 9. Nxe4 Bf5, etc.¹) 8... dxe4+ 9. Kc4 whereupon Black should not continue with 9... Be6+ 10. Kb4 e3+ 11. Ka3 Nc6 since White replies with 12. b3 followed by Kb2, but rather with 9... e3+! 10. Kb3 Nc6 11. a3 Be6+ and wins. This illustrates the method of countering a king's planned withdrawal to safety.
zh: 白方计划b3后接Kb2。如果7. Nc3，则7... Nf6! 8. Qe1（或8. Qf3 dxe4+ 9. Nxe4 Bf5等¹）8... dxe4+ 9. Kc4，此时黑方不应继续9... Be6+ 10. Kb4 e3+ 11. Ka3 Nc6，因为白方可以12. b3后接Kb2；正确的是9... e3+! 10. Kb3 Nc6 11. a3 Be6+，黑方获胜。这说明了怎样阻止王按计划退到安全地带。

text: ¹ This line is only equal after 10. Qxf4 exf4 11. Ke2! Nxe4 12. d3 followed by Bxf4, restoring the material balance.
zh: ¹ 10. Qxf4 exf4 11. Ke2! Nxe4 12. d3后接Bxf4，白方恢复子力平衡，这个变化只是均势。

text: If 8. d4 then 8... Nc6 9. Bb5 (or 9. b3) 9... exd4+ and Black has three pawns for his bishop as well as good prospects for a continuing attack on White's king or, indeed, his knight on a4.
zh: 如果8. d4，则8... Nc6 9. Bb5（或9. b3）9... exd4+，黑方以一象换得三兵，而且有望继续攻击白王，甚至攻击a4上的白马。

caption_zh: 白方走完9. a3后的局面

text: 9. c4? would be weak because of 9... b5!. Similarly, 9. Bxa6 bxa6 10. c3 Qxg2 11. Qf3 (or 11. Ne2 Bg4 12. Re1 Ne7!) 11... Qh3! is bad for White.² This is a typical example of an attack against a displaced king being deferred on the grounds that further action would only help the consolidation of the king's position. Thus, for example, after 9. Bxa6 bxa6 10. c3, 10... Rb8+ would enable White to prepare a new home for his king on b2 by 11. Ka3 and b3. Instead, Black directs his attack against the other flank and, while mowing down some pawns, tries to exploit the general lack of development of White's position.
zh: 9. c4?较弱，因为9... b5!。同样，9. Bxa6 bxa6 10. c3 Qxg2 11. Qf3（或11. Ne2 Bg4 12. Re1 Ne7!）11... Qh3!对白方不利。² 这是推迟攻击暴露的王的典型例子：继续追击只会帮助王稳固位置。例如9. Bxa6 bxa6 10. c3之后，10... Rb8+会让白方通过11. Ka3和b3，在b2为王安排一个新家。黑方因此转向另一侧进攻，一边扫荡白兵，一边设法利用白方整体出子不足。

text: ² This is highly disputable after 12. Qg3 Qxh1 13. Qxe5+ Kf8 14. Nxh3, and White could quickly develop a strong initiative.
zh: ² 12. Qg3 Qxh1 13. Qxe5+ Kf8 14. Nxh3之后，上述判断很值得商榷；白方可以很快形成强大的主动权。

text: Effective, and probably necessary, although it gives no more than a draw. If 9... Be6 White would reply 10. d4! exd4 11. Bxa6 bxa6 12. Nf3 with the better prospects. Bilguer's Handbuch answers 9... Be6 with 10. d3? d4+ 11. c4 dxc3+ 12. Kxc3 and considers that White retains the advantage. However, after 12... Qd4+ 13. Kd2 Nf6! 14. Qc2 (if he stops 14... Ne4+ by 14. Nc3, then 14... Nc5!) 14... O-O-O 15. Nf3 Qf2+ 16. Kd1 Ng4 Black has excellent chances based on ...e4 and ...Ne3+.
zh: 有力，而且很可能是必需的一步，虽然最多只能取得和棋。如果9... Be6，白方可以10. d4! exd4 11. Bxa6 bxa6 12. Nf3，前景较好。比尔格的《开局谱》给9... Be6的应对是10. d3? d4+ 11. c4 dxc3+ 12. Kxc3，并认为白方仍有优势。然而12... Qd4+ 13. Kd2 Nf6! 14. Qc2（如果14. Nc3阻止14... Ne4+，则14... Nc5!）14... O-O-O 15. Nf3 Qf2+ 16. Kd1 Ng4之后，黑方以...e4和...Ne3+为基础，机会很好。

text: 10. Kxa4 Nc5+ 11. Kb4 a5+ 12. Kxc5
zh: 10. Kxa4 Nc5+ 11. Kb4 a5+ 12. Kxc5

text: If 12. Kc3? then 12... d4+ 13. Kc4 b6 14. Kd5 f6 15. Kc6 Kd8, and the mating net is complete.²
zh: 如果12. Kc3?，则12... d4+ 13. Kc4 b6 14. Kd5 f6 15. Kc6 Kd8，杀网已经织成。²

text: ¹ In his book Draw!, Wolfgang Heidenfeld offered some rather convincing analysis to prove that White could have won by 11. Kb5!.
zh: ¹ 沃尔夫冈·海登费尔德在《和棋！》中给出了颇有说服力的分析，证明白方可以通过11. Kb5!获胜。

text: ² Heidenfeld pointed out that this line can be improved by 14. Qf3 Be6+ 15. Qd5 Ne7 16. Qxe6 fxe6 with an unclear position.
zh: ² 海登费尔德指出，这个变化可以改进为14. Qf3 Be6+ 15. Qd5 Ne7 16. Qxe6 fxe6，局面不明朗。

caption_zh: 白方走完14. Bc6后的局面

text: The only reply!
zh: 唯一的应对！

text: Against 16. c3? or 16. Ka4?, 16... Nd4 is decisive.
zh: 对16. c3?或16. Ka4?，16... Nd4都是决定性的。

text: He must not capture! If 17. Kxb7? then 17... Kd7 18. Qg4+ Kd6 and White has no defence against 19... Rhb8#.
zh: 不能吃象！如果17. Kxb7?，则17... Kd7 18. Qg4+ Kd6，白方无法防住19... Rhb8#。

text: Black keeps up perpetual check with the bishop on b7 and a6. White's king must not venture to a4 because of ...Bc4 and then ...b5#. An original ending to a king hunt!
zh: 黑象在b7和a6之间往返，形成长将。白王不能冒险走到a4，因为黑方有...Bc4后接...b5#。一场追王竟以如此独特的方式结束！

text: The next game abounds in dramatic features and gives us an opportunity for some more remarks on the subject of attacking a king that has lost the right to castle.
zh: 下一盘棋充满戏剧性，也给了我们进一步讨论如何攻击失去易位权利的王的机会。

text:
Morphy – Barnes
Simultaneous Display against Five Masters, London 1859
Petroff Defence
zh:
墨菲—巴恩斯
1859年，伦敦，对五位大师的车轮战
俄罗斯防御

text: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bc4
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bc4

text: Morphy regularly employed this against the Petroff; it does no more than leave the position evenly balanced.
zh: 墨菲经常用这步棋应对俄罗斯防御；它并不能带来更多，只能保持均势。

text: A dubious gambit originating from Kieseritzky.
zh: 这是基塞里茨基提出的一种可疑的弃兵。

text: 4... Nxc3 5. dxc3 f6!
zh: 4... Nxc3 5. dxc3 f6!

text: A good, as well as necessary, move in this position.
zh: 在这个局面中，这步既好，也必需。

text: 6. O-O Qe7?!
zh: 6. O-O Qe7?!

text: After this White has approximately equal chances. Correct was 6... Nc6! 7. Nh4 g6 8. f4 f5! with advantage to Black.
zh: 这之后白方大致可以保持均势。正确的是6... Nc6! 7. Nh4 g6 8. f4 f5!，黑方有利。

text: 7. Nh4 d6 8. Qh5+ Kd8 9. f4
zh: 7. Nh4 d6 8. Qh5+ Kd8 9. f4

text: 9. Ng6? fails against 9... Qe8.
zh: 9. Ng6?会被9... Qe8反驳。

text: 9... Be6 10. Bxe6 Qxe6 11. fxe5 dxe5 12. Ng6
zh: 9... Be6 10. Bxe6 Qxe6 11. fxe5 dxe5 12. Ng6

text: White regains the pawn, since if 12... Qe8?, then 13. Qd1+! unpins the knight with gain of tempo.
zh: 白方吃回一兵，因为如果12... Qe8?，则13. Qd1+!带着先手解除马的牵制。

text: A positional mistake, since he forfeits the chance of c4, without which his pawn attack is ineffective. 16. a4 was correct.
zh: 这是位置上的错误，因为白方放弃了c4的机会；没有这步冲兵，兵的攻击就缺乏力量。正确的是16. a4。

text: Threatening ...Nf8.
zh: 威胁...Nf8。

text: 18. Qg4 Qe6 19. Qe4 Nb6! (D)
zh: 18. Qg4 Qe6 19. Qe4 Nb6!（见图）
caption_zh: 黑方走完19... Nb6后的局面

text: Owing to the weakness on c4, White's position has lost its sting. Morphy now decides to compromise his game still further by sacrificing his knight; there is probably nothing better.
zh: 由于c4的弱点，白方的局面已经失去锋芒。墨菲现在决定弃马，使自己的局面进一步恶化；大概也没有更好的办法。

text: 20. Qxb7 Qg4 21. a4 Rc8 22. Rad1 Qxg6 23. Be3 Nc4 24. Qc6 Qf7
zh: 20. Qxb7 Qg4 21. a4 Rc8 22. Rad1 Qxg6 23. Be3 Nc4 24. Qc6 Qf7

text: Clearly not 24... Nxe3 because of 25. Rxd6+ Ke7 26. Rd7+ Kf8 27. Qc5+.
zh: 显然不能24... Nxe3，因为25. Rxd6+ Ke7 26. Rd7+ Kf8 27. Qc5+。

text: 25. Bxa7 e4
zh: 25. Bxa7 e4

text: 25... Ke7 would also have been good, followed by ...Kf8 (“delayed artificial castling”).
zh: 25... Ke7也很好，随后...Kf8，完成“姗姗来迟的人工易位”。

text: 26. Rd4 Qh5
zh: 26. Rd4 Qh5

text: Black begins to have his threats. 27. h3 is obviously met by 27... Qe5, while if 27. g3, then 27... Rh8 28. h4 Qe2, threatening mate by either 29... Qxf1+ or 29... Rxh4+. Morphy now finds the one reply which still offers resistance.
zh: 黑方开始制造威胁。27. h3显然可以用27... Qe5应对；如果27. g3，则27... Rh8 28. h4 Qe2，威胁通过29... Qxf1+或29... Rxh4+将杀。墨菲找到了唯一仍能抵抗的应对。

caption_zh: 黑方走完28... e2后的局面

text: 28... Qh4 was probably even stronger.
zh: 28... Qh4很可能更强。

text: Black has drawn his opponent's king out of position but now, when he is faced with the task of producing a mating attack, he stumbles. 31... f5? only appears to tighten the net (that is, by the threat of 32... Qf1+ 33. Rxf1 Rxh2#); in fact it allows the king to escape via g5. 31... Qf1+ 32. Rxf1 Rxh2+ 33. Kg4 Ne5+ would also have been unsound, since after 34. Kg3! Nxc6+ White can liquidate by interpolating 35. Rxd6+ cxd6 36. Bb6+ and only then 37. Kxh2.
zh: 黑方已经把对手的王引了出来，但在需要发动将杀进攻时却失误了。31... f5?只是表面上收紧杀网——威胁32... Qf1+ 33. Rxf1 Rxh2#；实际上却让白王可以经g5逃脱。31... Qf1+ 32. Rxf1 Rxh2+ 33. Kg4 Ne5+也不成立，因为34. Kg3! Nxc6+之后，白方可以插入35. Rxd6+ cxd6 36. Bb6+，然后才37. Kxh2，通过兑换化解局面。

text: 31... Qxc3+ 32. Rd3 (forced) 32... Qe5 33. Qf3 Ke7, etc. was one line which led to victory.
zh: 31... Qxc3+ 32. Rd3（被迫）32... Qe5 33. Qf3 Ke7等，是一条可以取胜的变化。

text: 32. Qxc4! Qf1+ 33. Kh4 Rxh2+ 34. Kg5 Qg2+?
zh: 32. Qxc4! Qf1+ 33. Kh4 Rxh2+ 34. Kg5 Qg2+?

text: After this fresh mistake Black ought to have lost. 34... Qg1+ 35. Rg4 Qe3+ might still have resulted in a win.¹
zh: 又犯了这个错误后，黑方本该输棋。34... Qg1+ 35. Rg4 Qe3+则仍有可能取胜。¹

text: ¹ In fact, it wins rather easily after 36. Kg6 Qh6+ 37. Kxf5 Qxh5+ 38. Rg5 Rf2+ 39. Rf4 Rxf4+ 40. Qxf4 Qf7+. It follows that White should have played 32. Rxc4! instead of 32. Qxc4?, when the position would indeed have been unclear.
zh: ¹ 实际上，36. Kg6 Qh6+ 37. Kxf5 Qxh5+ 38. Rg5 Rf2+ 39. Rf4 Rxf4+ 40. Qxf4 Qf7+后，黑方取胜相当容易。由此可见，白方应该走32. Rxc4!，而不是32. Qxc4?；那样局面才真正不明朗。

caption_zh: 白方走完35. Rg4后的局面

text: By sacrificing his rook White succeeds in blocking the g-file and thus obtaining a respite for his king in the comparative safety of g5. Naturally, the king is only secure there for one or two moves, but in the present position that is enough, for White also has some threats at his disposal.
zh: 白方弃车，成功堵住g线，让王在相对安全的g5获得喘息。当然，王在那里只能安全地待上一两步，但在当前局面中已经足够，因为白方也有一些可以制造的威胁。

text: The initiative now passes to White, and he should win quickly. The creation of a “makeshift shelter” for one or two moves is often extremely important when the king is being pursued, always on the assumption, of course, that the counterattack made possible by the gain of time promises to be successful.
zh: 主动权现在转到白方手中，他应当很快获胜。王被追赶时，为它安排一个能停留一两步的“临时避难所”，往往极其重要。当然，前提始终是：利用赢得的时间发动反击，必须有成功的希望。

text: Fortune smiled on him earlier, but now he loses the game which he could have won, e.g. 36. Rxd6+ cxd6 37. Qg8+ Ke7 (if 37... Kc7 or 37... Kd7, then 38. Qf7+ Kc6 39. b5#) 38. Qxg7+ Ke8 (or 38... Ke6 39. Qf6+ Kd5 40. Qf7+! mating next move) 39. Qg6+ Ke7 (if 39... Kd7 then 40. Qf7+ Kd8 41. Bb6+ Rc7 42. Qxc7+ Ke8 43. Qd8+ Kf7 44. Qf6+ Kg8 45. Qg6+ Kf8 46. Qxd6+, etc.) 40. Qf6+ Ke8 41. Qe6+ Kd8 42. Bb6+ Rc7 43. Qxd6+, etc.
zh: 之前幸运之神曾眷顾白方，现在他却输掉了本来可以获胜的对局。例如36. Rxd6+ cxd6 37. Qg8+ Ke7（如果37... Kc7或37... Kd7，则38. Qf7+ Kc6 39. b5#）38. Qxg7+ Ke8（或38... Ke6 39. Qf6+ Kd5 40. Qf7+!，下一步将杀）39. Qg6+ Ke7（如果39... Kd7，则40. Qf7+ Kd8 41. Bb6+ Rc7 42. Qxc7+ Ke8 43. Qd8+ Kf7 44. Qf6+ Kg8 45. Qg6+ Kf8 46. Qxd6+等）40. Qf6+ Ke8 41. Qe6+ Kd8 42. Bb6+ Rc7 43. Qxd6+等。

text: If 37. Qf8+ then 37... Qe8 38. Rxd6+ cxd6 39. Qxd6+ Qd7 40. Bb6+ Ke8 41. Qxh2 Qe7+ and Black captures the bishop by further checking.
zh: 如果37. Qf8+，则37... Qe8 38. Rxd6+ cxd6 39. Qxd6+ Qd7 40. Bb6+ Ke8 41. Qxh2 Qe7+，黑方继续将军，随后吃掉白象。

text: Barnes played a number of games against Morphy; with his distinctive positional style, he was the most successful of all the British masters against that combinative genius.
zh: 巴恩斯与墨菲下过多盘棋；凭借独特的位置型风格，他在所有英国大师中，对这位组合天才取得了最好的战绩。

text: Now comes the third and last example from the collection of curiosities – the game between Michelet and Kieseritzky, in which the hunted white king is not only saved but goes on actively to participate in the attack on his black colleague. The key to this success is the confinement of Black's queen in a most unusual “cage”.
zh: 接下来是这组奇闻中的第三个、也是最后一个例子：米舍莱对基塞里茨基一局。被追赶的白王不仅获救，还积极参与了对黑王的进攻。成功的关键，是把黑后关进了一个极不寻常的“笼子”。

text:
Michelet – Kieseritzky
Paris, 1845
King's Gambit Accepted
zh:
米舍莱—基塞里茨基
1845年，巴黎
接受王翼弃兵

text: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 g5 4. Bc4 g4 5. Ne5
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 g5 4. Bc4 g4 5. Ne5

text: Today the Muzio Gambit 5. O-O is considered more promising.
zh: 在作者写作时，5. O-O的穆齐奥弃兵被认为更有希望。

text: The so-called Cochrane Gambit, which is favourable for Black.
zh: 这就是所谓的科克伦弃兵，对黑方有利。

text: 7. d4 Nf6 8. Nc3 Bg7
zh: 7. d4 Nf6 8. Nc3 Bg7

text: 8... fxg2+ is also good.
zh: 8... fxg2+也很好。

text: 9. g3 Qh3+ 10. Kf2 d6 11. Nxf7 Rf8 12. Ng5 Qg2+ 13. Ke3 (D)
zh: 9. g3 Qh3+ 10. Kf2 d6 11. Nxf7 Rf8 12. Ng5 Qg2+ 13. Ke3（见图）
caption_zh: 白方走完13. Ke3后的局面

text: An unsound idea, since White can obviously counter it by Kd3, after which the bishop will have done nothing but lose control of the long diagonal. 13... Nc6 was correct, and if 14. a3 then 14... Ke7 threatening 15... h6.
zh: 这个构想不成立，因为白方显然可以Kd3应对，黑象除了失去对长斜线的控制之外，什么也没有做到。正确的是13... Nc6，如果14. a3，则14... Ke7，威胁15... h6。

text: 14. Kd3 Nc6 15. a3 Bxg5 16. Bxg5 Nxe4
zh: 14. Kd3 Nc6 15. a3 Bxg5 16. Bxg5 Nxe4

text: This sacrifice is incorrect, but Black's position was already inferior as a result of his mistake on the 13th move. White's king is quite happy on d3.
zh: 这次弃子不正确，但黑方第13步的错误已经使局面变差。白王在d3相当舒适。

text: 17. Qe1 Bf5 18. Nxe4 f2 19. Qe3 Kd7 20. Bd5 Rae8 21. Raf1!
zh: 17. Qe1 Bf5 18. Nxe4 f2 19. Qe3 Kd7 20. Bd5 Rae8 21. Raf1!

text: White actually encourages Black to carry out his threat to win the queen, producing an original riposte to it.
zh: 白方实际上鼓励黑方执行得后的威胁，并为此准备了独特的反击。

text: 21... Bxe4+ 22. Bxe4 Rf3 23. Qxf3! gxf3 24. Bf5+
zh: 21... Bxe4+ 22. Bxe4 Rf3 23. Qxf3! gxf3 24. Bf5+

text: White now wins the other rook, leaving the black queen boxed in at g2. White conducts the ending with what is in effect an extra piece and, logically enough, takes his king into battle as well.
zh: 白方现在要吃掉另一只黑车，而黑后被困在g2。白方进入残局后，实际上相当于多一子；他顺理成章地也把王投入了战斗。

text: 24... Re6 25. d5 Ne5+ 26. Ke4 h5 27. dxe6+ Ke8 28. Bf6 h4 29. Bxe5 dxe5 30. Kxe5 hxg3 31. Kf6 1-0
zh: 24... Re6 25. d5 Ne5+ 26. Ke4 h5 27. dxe6+ Ke8 28. Bf6 h4 29. Bxe5 dxe5 30. Kxe5 hxg3 31. Kf6 1-0

text: The final position deserves a diagram.
